title: Object representing a presheaf of sets, with its universal object
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $F:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ a functor, written $F(g):F(V)\to F(V')$ for a morphism $g:V'\to V$ of $\mathcal C$. A pair $(U,\xi)$ of an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and an element $\xi\in F(U)$ *represents* $F$, and $\xi$ is called the *universal object*, if for every object $V$ of $\mathcal C$ the map $\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)\to F(V)$, $f\mapsto F(f)(\xi)$, is a bijection; $U$ is then called an object *representing* $F$.
